title: Audio signal chain
goal: Show the ordered studio audio path from input through processing to monitor output.

rubric.must: A continuous path visibly runs from Audio Input to Monitor Speaker.
Preamp, high-pass filter, EQ, DSP, DAC, and amplifier appear in the correct visible order.
Connections visibly label balanced analogue, digital, analogue line, and speaker-level signals.
Input and output blocks are visually differentiated from processing blocks.
The chain is laid out as a clear left-to-right signal flow.

ideal.notes: Drawn by `scripts/visual-eval/draw-blockdiagram-target.mjs`, which draws all eight cases from one kit so the set is one drawing repeated. A functional block diagram of Audio Signal Chain. 8 blocks carry the forward signal path, folded into 2 rows joined by a labelled channel so the chain stays readable. Every wire is orthogonal, every arrowhead lands on a block edge, signal names are set in italic beside the wire they name, and a legend at the foot states the line codes. Drawn in the idiom of the block-diagram exemplar (`visual-eval/exemplars/blockdiagram/ideal.svg`): ink outlines, block labels at 13 over at most two lines, signal names in italic slate beside the wire they name, a 34 px summing junction with its signs set just outside the circle, a filled dot at every pickoff, orthogonal wires only, and terracotta spent on nothing but the measured/feedback path. A long chain is folded into bands joined by a labelled channel, the exemplar's own solution to a chain too long for one row. One extension of the exemplar: each block body carries a pale fill keyed to the `role:` the DSL declares for it — input, control, actuator, plant, sensor, output — with a swatch legend at the foot. The exemplar leaves every body white, which discards information the author supplied on every single block; the fills are kept pale and the outlines ink so terracotta remains the loudest thing on the page and still means only one thing. Routing picks whichever corner misses every other block, and the checker tests each label against every other label, every block body, every wire segment and the canvas edge, plus every wire against every block body: 0 overlaps and no wire runs through a block.
